assertion_analysis.fails_if: A synthetic run pointer exists in the real pointer directory before or after a case, including a fixture isolation regression.
The code omits, duplicates, reorders or changes an ID sent to squeue; this captures the actual subprocess vector rather than echoing a supplied observation.
The real classifier declares the live-batch fixture abandoned or sets producer_gone evidence despite the scheduler returning its middle job.
The classifier keeps the all-absent batch waiting instead of returning its existing producer-gone classification.
The emitted stillness evidence is below the required bound; restoring batch omission alone does not make this supporting assertion fail.
The row drops or changes the independently supplied batch IDs, as the recorded extraction mutation does.
The all-absent row omits the measured scheduler absence or incorrectly claims the scheduler was not consulted.
The no-job fixture triggers a scheduler query or emits scheduler job evidence.
The no-job fixture ceases to use the existing abandonment classification after its stillness bound.
The no-job row omits nonconsultation or restores the unsupported no-live-job wording.
A single bare script number starts being recognized or queried as a scheduler job.
The single-number fixture stays waiting or loses the nonconsultation explanation.
The 80,443 port list becomes job IDs, reaches squeue or appears in scheduler evidence; five-digit port lists are not tested.
The short-port fixture stays waiting or loses its nonconsultation explanation.
The absent-command or failed-command path does not attempt exactly the three derived job IDs.
An unaskable query is treated as proof of abandonment.
The unaskable row omits its scheduler uncertainty and three-job context, falsely asserts no live job, or calls the run process producer.
Any of the four exercised detail variants again contains the word producer.
The classifier binds a different reader or defines one locally; these are structural reuse assertions, not proof it invokes that reader correctly.
The sacct-job absence path loses the run-own-process wording.
The no-job abandoned-wait row loses the run-own-process wording.

assertion_independence: No tautological comparison found: BATCH_JOBS is an input fixture, but the opposite sides are the subprocess vector captured from real parsing or the actual classifier output; removing extraction demonstrably changes them. Identity/source assertions are counted only as structural checks.

findings.text: blocking: The five-digit cutoff is not a valid distinction between jobs and ports: the same module defines ports through 65535 at :691, so nc -z host 50000,50001 is misread as two jobs, while a script given 1234,5678 names no jobs despite the plan's two-or-more rule; the latter can still become producer-gone while one job is alive, and the former can retain a dead wait on unrelated scheduler work.

blocking: For an interpreter vector such as ["python", "/path/wait_jobs.py", "--jobs=1312389,1312390"], the raw-list pass rejects the prefixed token and _wait_probe_program_words splits it at the comma, leaving only 1312389 attached to --jobs; 1312390 is never queried, so when only that second job is alive the wait can still become producer-gone; glued -j1312389,1312390 has the same truncation.

non-blocking: _absent_pid, _stamp and _history duplicate tests/test_a_run_parked_on_a_live_job_keeps_waiting.py:79-93, and _waiting_run duplicates its :96 parked-run constructor with script additions; these additions duplicate the existing fixture capability rather than extending or wrapping its owner, so shared fixture changes can drift between the two modules.

non-blocking: The committed receipt still states 70 head passes, six added cases, a 2-failed/3-passed mutation and 724 importer head passes; the final revision's logs instead record 73 passes with two setup errors, nine added cases, 4 failed/69 passed/two setup errors for the mutation and 727 importer head passes, so the versioned evidence does not describe the reviewed revision accurately.

gate_evidence.positive_control: The same failure reader found both inventory setup errors in each armed log; this is a measured empty difference, not an empty input.
